identity.title: Support for fragile porous dust in a gravitationally self-regulated disk around IM Lup

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here we present a physical model of the IM Lup disk that offers a comprehensive explanation for diverse observations spanning from near-infrared to millimeter wavelengths.

question.value: Can a gravitationally self-regulated disk model with fragile, porous dust and accretion heating explain the IM Lup disk observations from near-infrared to millimeter wavelengths?

evidence.quote: we develop a theoretical model of dust evolution in the gravitationally self-regulated (GSR) disk around IM Lup.

findings_qualitative.value: Fragile dust (vf ≲ 1 m/s) and moderate porosity (f~0.2) explain mm and polarization data; accretion heating explains inner brightness and 100 au shadow.

evidence.quote: Our findings underscore the importance of dust fragility in retaining the observed millimeter emission

claims.hypothesis: Dust must be fragile to reproduce mm emission in a GSR disk
claims.experiment: Compare DustPy+RADMC-3D models with MAPS/DSHARP intensity
claims.result: vf ≲ 1 m/s within 70% up to 200 au; 130% for 3 and ~1000% for 10 m/s

evidence.quote: aligns with the observations within a relative difference of 70% up to 200 au

claims.experiment: Compare synthetic polarization with Band 6/7 data
claims.result: Porous 0.85-0.40% at Band 7 vs compact 0.42-0.10%; observed ~1%

evidence.quote: the porous model with smaller $v_{\rm f}$ is more consistent with the observations

claims.hypothesis: Pebble accretion can form a planet at 100 au
claims.experiment: Pebble accretion growth timescale for 3 Earth-mass

evidence.loc: 5.1 Planet formation in the IM Lup disk
evidence.quote: the growth timescale is $\gtrsim10^{7}$ yr at 100 au, which is much longer than the age of IM Lup.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust composition uncertain; MRI/wind accretion not modeled; model underestimates intensity beyond 200 au
